title: The Concept of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance describes the mental stress experienced by a person who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values. This discomfort arises when an individual's actions contradict their established self-image or belief system.

The magnitude of this dissonance is often determined by the importance of the cognitions involved; highly valued beliefs will create stronger reactions to inconsistency. To alleviate this uncomfortable state, individuals are motivated to change one of the conflicting elements, modify a belief, or introduce a new consonant cognition (rationalization).

Research indicates that resolution strategies can take various forms. These include seeking out information that supports the existing behavior while downplaying contradictory evidence, minimizing the perceived threat of the conflict, or altering behavior to align with internal values.
